ConocoPhillips edged up 0.23% today to $137.35, extending a 6% rally over two weeks as oil prices remain elevated and geopolitical tensions persist. U.S. crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel while global oil sits at $109.51—a wide gap reflecting Middle East supply concerns. Recent shipping strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passage for oil exports, have kept the market on edge despite diplomatic efforts by China and India to broker peace between Iran and Gulf nations.

The stock's steady climb reflects oil traders pricing in sustained supply risk. While some traders briefly hoped for a resolution after comments about potential negotiations, Iran's leadership has signaled no surrender, and the latest vessel strike suggests the geopolitical friction remains real enough to support higher oil prices—which directly benefit an oil producer's revenues and earnings.
